sentences.text: Tynskya is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the family Messelasturidae.
The genus Tynskya was first described in 2000 by the paleontologist Gerald Mayr.

The type species Tynskya eocaena was named based on an incomplete articulated skeleton found in the Tynsky quarry within the Green River Formation of Wyoming, USA. The genus name honors the Tynsky quarry where the type specimen was discovered, while the species epithet eocaena refers to the time period in which the animal lived.

A second species, Tynskya waltonensis, was described in 2021 based on a partial skeleton. The holotype for this species was originally discovered in 1986 by Paul Bergdhal in Walton-on-the-Naze, England, within the London Clay formation.

Two additional species, Tynskya crassitarsus and Tynskya brevitarsus, were described in 2023 based on partial skeletons. The species name T. crassitarsus refers to its thick tarsometatarsus, while T. brevitarsus refers to its short tarsometatarsus.
Tynskya lived during the Ypresian stage, approximately 56 to 48.07 million years ago.

Isolated bones of Tynskya have been found in the London Clay formation. Fossils of the type species Tynskya eocaena are known from the Green River Formation in North America. The species Tynskya waltonensis, Tynskya brevitarsus, and Tynskya crassitarsus are found in the Walton Member of the London Clay Formation in England.
